take: Black Sea oil shipping insurance costs have surged from roughly $200,000 to $2.5 million per vessel, a direct tax on crude delivered out of the region that will widen differentials and push buyers towards alternative Atlantic Basin barrels. The tanker war is spreading across the Gulf, with a drone strike off Oman leaving two Indian seafarers missing and a second tanker hit by a projectile, whilst the ClarkSea Index jumped 12% in a week to a record $84,951 a day — freight is now the binding constraint on crude and product arbitrage, not the flat price. Positioning-wise, the orderbook bunker demand story is quietly bullish for residual fuel, with implied demand from ships on order up 10% since July to 64 million mtoe a year, even as methanol slips and conventional oil still dominates. The cross-market link to watch is gasoil versus bunker: with Russian diesel release talk dragging oil lower, any further Iran escalation would invert that and pull VLSFO and gasoil higher together, squeezing the Hi-5 spread. Over the next 24 hours, watch whether the Oman and Gulf incidents escalate into a broader war-risk premium across the Arabian Sea, and whether the rumoured Russian diesel release actually lands — both will set the tone for products cracks into the European open.
